learningObjective: Reason about correctness testing (tolerance-based) and honest steady-state benchmarking (warmup + sync + CUDA events).

canonicalClaims.claim: Reliable Triton kernel benchmarking requires (i) warmup runs, (ii) `cudaDeviceSynchronize` before and after the timed region, and (iii) CUDA events for GPU-side timing. Correctness testing compares against a reference with tolerance appropriate to the dtype and op (e.g., `torch.testing.assert_close`).
conditions: CUDA async execution model; FP arithmetic is not bit-reproducible in general.
nonImplications: Does not imply CUDA events are the only timing method.
Does not imply steady-state is the only metric; compile time should also be reported.

misconceptions.claim: `time.time()` on a single launch is a reliable microbenchmark.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Async launches skew the measurement; single-shot has high variance.

misconceptions.claim: JIT compile / autotune time should be included in per-iteration latency.
misconceptions.whyWrong: One-time compile cost is separately reported, not amortized into per-iter numbers.

misconceptions.claim: Bitwise comparison (`torch.equal`) is the correct correctness check for FP kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP kernels are order-dependent; tolerance-based comparison is required.

misconceptions.claim: Warmup runs are unnecessary because Triton kernels have no lazy state.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPU clock ramp, cache warm-up, and driver/runtime state all benefit from warmup.
